precise_statement.evidence: Candidate states Z(X)=sum chi(P)/sqrt(labels) for a fixed quadratic Dirichlet character on rational primes and the matched polynomial Dirichlet character on F_q[t] irreducibles.

finite_field_anchor.evidence: F_q[t] side is exact: chi(P) is the quadratic residue character modulo a fixed irreducible quadratic polynomial M_q(t), checked across q=3,5,7 degree ladders.

integer_holdout.evidence: Integer side checks the preregistered ladder 1000000, 2000000, 4000000, 8000000 through N=8000000.

controls.evidence: No control-surviving matched profile: integerBeatsControls=false, signsAligned=true, profileSpread=2.209918.

compression.evidence: Low-parameter object: one integer quadratic character, one fixed irreducible quadratic modulus per q, and one normalized cumulative character sum.

scale_stability.evidence: Scale gate requires complete integer and field ladders plus a matched control-surviving profile. Integer ladder=true; field ladders=true; matchedProfile=false.

novelty_audit.evidence: The object is a real new domain after the algebraic-family stop, but the observed small character-race sums are standard Dirichlet/PNT-in-progressions calibration and do not beat nearby-character controls.

reproducibility.evidence: JSON/MD/SVG/script artifacts are present for the 8M quadratic Dirichlet race run.

proof_path.evidence: The proof path is classical calibration: Dirichlet characters and prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions on Z, polynomial Dirichlet characters and prime polynomial theorem on F_q[t].

expert_pack.evidence: No expert-ready breakthrough pack exists because controls, novelty, and matched-profile gates fail; this is a calibration artifact.

theoremShape.statistic: Z(X)=sum chi(P)/sqrt(labels), with chi a fixed quadratic Dirichlet character
theoremShape.integer: P ranges over rational primes p<=N and chi(p)=(p/m) for fixed odd prime modulus m.
theoremShape.functionField: P ranges over monic irreducibles in F_q[t] and chi(P) is the quadratic residue character modulo a fixed irreducible quadratic M_q(t).
theoremShape.baseline: Dirichlet prime number theorem / prime polynomial theorem in arithmetic progressions predicts cancellation; promotion requires a residual beyond nearby-character and random controls.
